segment: Public, non-profit and grant-funded e-mobility fleets in LA (LACI, Clean Mobility Options, Metro, LADOT, LA28, city and county pilots)
summary: Small, slow and mostly closed for 2026-27. The one big LA e-bike fleet purchase (LACI South Central Power Up, 250 'brand new, custom' pedal-assist e-bikes, CARB STEP via LADOT UBM) was made in 2024 for a two-year pilot; the supplier is not named on any LACI, LADOT or program page and no vehicle RFP is posted on laincubator.org/pilots. Clean Mobility Options is closed ('additional CMO funding opportunities are currently closed'); CARB's STEP page returned no content through the proxy and no 2026 LA round surfaced. The only live, vendor-open money is the SGVCOG GoSGV $2,000 e-cargo-bike voucher (round 2 of 450 vouchers opened 29 Apr 2026, next review Fall 2026; ~900 vouchers remaining) which requires Class 1-3, 750 W max, 330 lb gross load rating and UL 2849 and/or EN 15194 certification and redemption at an approved San Gabriel Valley bike shop (retailer sign-up form exists). Mobility Wallet Phase III (2026, Caltrans + federal ATTAIN) is a prepaid-card consumer subsidy spendable at bike shops, i.e. HMP can be a merchant but not a fleet vendor. LA28's March 2026 procurement plan has no micromobility or two-wheel category; the nearest rows are Fleet Management Services (Q2-Q3 2026, $$$$), Vehicle Rental or Leasing Services (Q2 2027 and Q2 2028, $$$) and Transportation Planning (Q2 2026-Q3 2027); targets are 75% local / 25% small business, and HMP at 768 Ceres Ave would qualify as Hyper-Local (City of LA) and Micro Business (<=25 employees for manufacturers). Realistic 12-month unit potential from this segment: 0 base, 20-40 high case (a Power Up refresh or a CBO sub-grant), and only if INNO carries UL 2849 documentation.

key_facts.claim: LACI South Central Power Up launched 16 Apr 2024: 250 e-bikes rentable one month at a time at 7 locations, two-year initial pilot, funded by CARB through California Climate Investments (STEP) with LADOT; bikes described only as 'brand new, custom e-bikes'; supplier not named

Power Up host CBOs: People for Mobility Justice, Ride On! Bike Shop, RideWitUs, SCOPE, T.R.U.S.T South LA, Esperanza Community Housing, Mercado La Paloma, Labor Community Strategy Center, Community Services Unlimited

southcentralpowerup.com (page dated 6 Aug 2026) still advertises 'Free 1+ Month Rentals' of 'motor-powered pedal assist' bikes in select South Central zip codes; free period was to end 30 Sep 2024 with 'a low-cost pricing model' after; hub sites run by 'Community Management Partners'; bike brand not named

LADOT describes the Power Up fleet as 250 'electric pedal-assist bikes' lent free for up to a month, part of the South LA UBM pilot which also brings shared EV cars and an on-demand EV shuttle plus Metro fare subsidies for 2,000 residents

Mobility Wallet Phase I ran May 2023-Apr 2024: 1,000 low-income South LA residents got a prepaid debit card with $150/month usable on transit, rideshare, micromobility, taxis and purchases at bike shops; Phase II run with LA Metro; Phase III scheduled for 2026 with Caltrans and a federal ATTAIN grant
laincubator.org/pilots lists only South Central Power Up as a mobility pilot; no open vehicle RFP, pilot-partner call or vendor-selection process is published; general contact 213-358-6500

Clean Mobility Options: 'Additional Clean Mobility Options (CMO) funding opportunities are currently closed'; applications were processed by CALSTART first-come-first-served; LACI + HACLA + Pedal Movement received nearly $1M for four e-bike hubs at Rancho San Pedro (Good2Go Bikes: 18 e-bikes, 2 e-cargo bikes, off-grid charging hub)

GoSGV e-cargo-bike voucher (SGVCOG + ActiveSGV): $2,000 per voucher; round two of 450 vouchers opened 29 Apr 2026 with roughly 900 more available; funded by California Transportation Commission, SCAG, Metro (I-10 ExpressLanes toll revenue) and the Strategic Growth Council; qualifying bikes cost roughly $1,500-2,500; recipients must complete safety training and buy at an approved SGV bike shop

GoSGV eligible bike: 'Class 1, 2, or 3 e-bike', motor 'maximum of 750 watts', 'Minimum gross weight capacity/load of 330lbs', 'UL2849 and/or EN 15194 battery certification'; seven approved shops (Around the Cycle Pasadena, E-Bike Cyclery Monrovia and San Dimas, The Local Bikestand Pomona, Montebello Bicycles, Redondo E-Bikes, Velo Pasadena); shops apply via a Google form; next award period 'application reviews in Fall 2026'

LA28 Procurement Plan (March 2026): suppliers register at La28.SupplierOne.co and sourcing events post on RAMP LA; targets 75% of addressable spend to Greater LA and 25% to small business; definitions: Local = HQ or principal office in LA, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino or Ventura County; Hyper-Local = HQ or principal office in the City of Los Angeles; Small = meets SBA size standard; Micro = 10 or fewer employees (25 or fewer for manufacturing)

LA28 category timing (projection as of March 2026): Fleet Management Services Q2 '26 and Q3 '26 ($$$$); Transportation Planning Services Q2 '26 and Q3 '27 ($$$$); Transportation Storage Service Q3 '26 ($$$$); Vehicle Rental or Leasing Services Q2 '27 and Q2 '28 ($$$); Public Transit Services Q3 '27 ($$$$); Taxicab Services Q1 '28 ($$$$). No bicycle, scooter, motorcycle or micromobility category appears
LA28 advises registering on RAMP LA and checking it at least every two weeks for RFIs and Expressions of Interest; registration does not guarantee a contract
Pacoima Beautiful Electro-Bici: 100 e-bikes, LADWP $500k; Long Beach 35-bike lending library operated by Propel; Santa Monica ZEDZ ended Dec 2022 (carried over from earlier research)

Cake, Ubco and other e-two-wheeler OEM failures (2024-25) mean grant-funded operators now weigh OEM solvency and parts continuity when choosing a supplier; a two-year-old brand with no UL 2849 paperwork is unlikely to be selected by a CARB sub-recipient that must document eligible vehicles

how_to_reach: LACI: apply to the incubator (laincubator.org) as an LA-based cleantech OEM 1 mile from campus; ask the Pilots team for the Power Up refresh timeline and the current e-bike vendor; no RFP exists, so this is relationship-first.

GoSGV: submit the retailer form on sgvcog.org/gosgv or, more realistically, get INNO onto the shelves of an approved SGV shop (Montebello Bicycles is closest to DTLA) before the Fall 2026 review; bring UL 2849 certificate and a 330 lb load rating sheet.

Mobility Wallet Phase III (2026): make sure HMP's LA store processes as a bike-shop merchant so card holders can spend $150/month on INNO rental or purchase; contact mobilitywallet@metro.net for merchant guidance.

LA28: register on La28.SupplierOne.co and RAMP LA now (free), tag as Hyper-Local + Micro + Small; watch for Fleet Management and Vehicle Rental/Leasing EOIs and approach the winning fleet prime as a two-wheel subcontractor.

CARB STEP / CMO: no open round; monitor ww2.arb.ca.gov STEP and cleanmobilityoptions.org; for-profits participate as vendors to a public/non-profit lead applicant, so line up Pedal Movement or a CBO as the applicant.
constraints: CARB-funded LA programs describe their bikes as 'pedal-assist'; California E-Bike Incentive Project and GoSGV accept Class 1-3 (throttle allowed on Class 2, 20 mph, 750 W) but require UL 2849 (system) and/or EN 15194 - INNO must carry the certificate, not just a UL 2271 battery cell cert (ASK HMP).
Grant sub-recipients must show competitive quotes and eligible-vehicle documentation; a moped-style Class 2 bike with no UL 2849 paperwork cannot be scored.
GoSGV redemption is limited to approved San Gabriel Valley shops; 768 Ceres Ave (DTLA) does not qualify as the point of sale.
LA28 has no two-wheel category; Fleet Management sourcing (Q2-Q3 2026) is already in progress; vehicle categories are services (rental/leasing) sourced Q2 2027.
MK.II and FLASH are motorcycles; no LA public program funds or lends motorcycles; they are irrelevant to this segment.
Public bodies pay net-30/60 and require COI (typically $1M GL) and W-9/vendor registration; LADOT site returned 403 through the proxy so the exact vendor forms were not read.
what_hmp_must_have: UL 2849 system certificate for INNO / LIVA (or EN 15194) and a written 330 lb gross-load rating - without it every program above is closed.
Registration on RAMP LA, La28.SupplierOne.co, Cal eProcure and SAM.gov; SBA small-business self-certification; City of LA business tax certificate at 768 Ceres Ave.
A 24-month fleet warranty letter and a parts-continuity statement (buyers cite Cake/Ubco).
Spanish-language rider materials and a safety-training module (GoSGV and Power Up require rider training).
A $1M/$2M general liability COI naming the public entity.

realistic_12mo_units.rationale: No open vehicle procurement in LA County for 2026-27 (CMO closed, no STEP round, Power Up bought in 2024, LA28 has no two-wheel category). High case = a Power Up refresh or a Phase III/ATTAIN-funded expansion where LACI or Pedal Movement buys 20-40 replacement bikes from a local UL-certified vendor, plus a handful of GoSGV voucher sales through an SGV shop. All contingent on UL 2849 documentation that HMP has not yet shown.

red_flags: Every dollar in this segment is grant money with fixed vehicle specs; INNO's eligibility is unproven (UL 2849, cargo rating).
The Power Up supplier is not public - if it is a national brand with a service contract, a refresh will go to the incumbent.
southcentralpowerup.com still shows 2024 copy in Aug 2026 (free period 'until 09/30/2024'), suggesting a program in maintenance mode rather than expansion.
LA28 spend is 75% local by target but categories are services; two-wheel vehicles would enter only through a fleet-management prime.
Time cost: public sales cycles run 6-18 months; the team should not staff this segment beyond registrations and one LACI relationship.
